detailed_rationale:
SAMHI Hotels owns and operates 31 hotels (4,904 rooms across 14 cities) under brands including Marriott, IHG, and Hyatt, with Tribute Portfolio and W Hotels properties upcoming. There is no promoter category in the current shareholding pattern (FIIs 44.6%, DIIs 17.4%, Public 38%) -- consistent with SAMHI's known ownership history as a private-equity-backed hotel-asset roll-up (Xander/ACIC and GIC-related investors), a structural feature of the business rather than a governance red flag by itself, but worth noting since there is no controlling promoter anchor.

The headline numbers require real scrutiny: FY26 net profit was reported at Rs.567 Cr versus Rs.86 Cr in FY25, and one quarter in the series showed an exceptional Rs.399 Cr profit (EPS Rs.15.92) versus a more normal Rs.48 Cr / EPS Rs.1.79 the prior quarter -- explicitly described in our research as 'anomalous and likely includes one-off gains,' consistent with the negative/volatile tax rates seen across periods, which point to deferred-tax-asset/loss-carryforward recognition rather than organic operating improvement. This is exactly the kind of earnings-quality one-off the analyst process is meant to catch: the resulting P/E of ~7.5-9.7x looks statistically cheap, and our own value score of 86.8 reflects that, but this is very likely a case of a low P/E manufactured by a one-off-inflated earnings denominator rather than genuine undervaluation. A cleaner read is ROCE of just 8.9% -- modest, not the return profile the headline PAT growth would suggest.

The sector backdrop is genuinely favorable: Indian hospitality has been in a multi-year structural upcycle (post-pandemic travel recovery, limited new supply growth), and SAMHI's own organic revenue grew a healthy 10% in FY26. But the company carries meaningful leverage (D/E ~0.85) with interest coverage explicitly flagged as low and no dividend paid. Reverse-DCF: on normalized (ex-one-off) earnings, the true multiple is materially higher than the ~7.5-9.7x headline, and against an 8.9% ROCE and elevated leverage, we do not see the current price as offering the margin of safety the low P/E superficially implies.
recommendation_rationale: The quant Sell (on both 3-year and 1-year views) holds up once the earnings-quality issue is priced in: the attractively low headline P/E is very likely a function of a one-off tax/DTA-driven profit spike rather than organic strength, and the cleaner ROCE (~8.9%) is unremarkable for a highly levered hotel-asset business with no dividend and flagged-low interest coverage. We are not fooled by the statistically cheap multiple and see no basis to rescue this to Hold.
summary: SAMHI Hotels owns a 31-hotel portfolio under global brands including Marriott, IHG, and Hyatt, benefiting from India's post-pandemic hospitality upcycle (organic revenue grew 10% in FY26). However, the company's reported profit has been dominated by large, one-off tax and deferred-tax-asset items in certain quarters, which makes the headline valuation (7.5-9.7 times earnings) look far cheaper than the underlying, normalized economics support -- return on capital employed is a modest 8.9% once you look past the one-offs. Combined with elevated leverage and no dividend, we rate this a Sell.
positive_para: India's hospitality sector is in a genuine structural upcycle with limited new room supply and strong post-pandemic travel demand, SAMHI's organic revenue grew a healthy 10% in FY26, and the portfolio carries strong global brand affiliations (Marriott, IHG, Hyatt) across 31 properties.
negative_para: A large share of reported FY26 and recent-quarter profit is attributable to one-off tax/deferred-tax-asset items rather than organic hotel operations -- explicitly flagged in our research as an anomalous, one-off-driven profit spike -- which makes the headline ~7.5-9.7x P/E and our own 86.8 value score misleading; the cleaner ROCE of just 8.9%, combined with elevated leverage, low flagged interest coverage, and no dividend, paints a much less attractive picture than the headline multiple suggests.
reverse_dcf_judgment: The headline 7.5-9.7x P/E is a one-off-earnings artifact, not a genuine bargain; normalizing for the tax/DTA-driven profit spikes, the effective multiple is materially higher, and against an 8.9% ROCE and elevated leverage, the price does not offer the margin of safety it appears to at first glance.
